description: Complete post-fix rerun of the declared CPU performance, memory and accuracy cohorts, plus CUDA comparisons and internal-solve dispatch neighbors. Original results remain immutable. Selection was expanded to the complete cohort because the final changes reach shared numerical and scheduling paths.
review_state: Reviewed: full comparison coverage retained; execute only after combined checks and a frozen release build.
selection_policy: Use one frozen release build and frozen harness source per host for the primary CPU comparisons; record all hashes before and after the run.
Preserve every original case ID, command, repeat count, thread budget, numerical gate, timeout, platform restriction and group. Duplicate original broad cases remain distinct observations.
Write correction results to a separate output directory with a new suite ID. Never overwrite or relabel the original failures, memory limits or slower cases.
Do not retry for a favorable timing outcome. Keep all results, including new regressions and unresolved upstream agreement failures.
Keep independent high-precision accuracy, physical invariants, cutoff sensitivity and upstream agreement as distinct evidence. Upstream disagreement is not itself proof of a native defect.

Run CUDA comparisons only after CPU measurements stop, using the same numerical source revision. CUDA numbers compare native CPU and native GPU paths; they do not imply an upstream treams GPU baseline.

changes_requiring_full_coverage.reason: Scaled small-matrix inversion affects sphere coefficients, assembled sphere scattering and coefficient pullbacks.
Equilibration decisions affect shared dense linear solves, including large-cutoff clusters.
Dense interaction pullbacks reuse allocations; public cluster, periodic and array reverse paths share this implementation.

Large systems with few internal illuminations use GMRES only after a deterministic contraction bound proves the assembled operator invertible, with unchanged residual tolerances and dense primal/adjoint fallbacks.
Small-argument cylindrical recurrence and scalar Jet arithmetic affect wave evaluations and derivative families.
Shared scalar ufunc scheduling and cylindrical dispatch changes require all registered function families and thread budgets.
Field and lattice derivative work is included across every declared forward and gradient series.
Chunked comparison checks preserve the same entrywise gates while reducing controller memory; corrected qualification handling reruns the complete original accuracy grid.

mac.thread_eligibility: Preserve original platforms fields: six 16-thread CPU cases are Linux only. GPU cases are Linux only.

original_guards_by_platform.explanation: Each case timeout overrides the original 900-second default. Memory limits are controller process-group RSS guards, not the reported worker peak RSS. Keep platform-specific invocation limits unchanged.

runtime_estimate.basis: Sum of original Linux controller elapsed times, including correctness checks, process startup and timing repeats. Not a promised completion time; changed kernels and previously stopped cases can change runtime.
runtime_estimate.new_boundary_estimate_basis: Thirty-two cases at approximately 2-6 seconds each, based on neighboring original internal-field case elapsed times; unmeasured until the rerun.
runtime_estimate.mac: Baseline requested-illumination cohort is still in progress. Completed groups plus the finished portion already exceed three hours; budget more than four hours for the complete rerun, and revise only after the full baseline completes.
runtime_estimate.excluded_from_estimate: Builds, static checks, Rust tests, CUDA device tests, WASM checks and any investigation after new failures.

unaffected_coverage.explanation: No declared CPU performance family is omitted after the shared scheduling and linear-algebra changes. GPU kernels are not intentionally changed, but their 20-case comparisons rerun for a fresh native CPU baseline and consistent source provenance.

required_functional_validation_before_ti.name: Native GPU device checks
required_functional_validation_before_ti.scope: The nine existing real-device Rust checks, using the configured CUDA environment. Do not rebuild or replace an extension during an active CPU cohort.

required_functional_validation_before_ti.name: WASM shared-core validation
required_functional_validation_before_ti.scope: WASM-target Clippy and browser-compatible numerical smoke checks through the existing Node script.
